Q: How to detect figures in a paper news image in Python? A:

I am not sure how robust it is. It works because the interior images are dark compared to the background color.

So here is the approach in Python OpenCV.

  • Read the input image

  • Threshold on the whitish background color and invert

  • Apply morphology open to isolate the interior images and remove noise

  • Get contours

  • Loop over the contours and do the following:

    • Get the contour area and bounding box

    • Draw the contours on a copy of the inpug

    • Filter the contours on area, width, height and aspect ratio (for squareness) to isolate the interior image regions

    • Draw those contours on a copy of the input

  • Save the images

Input image:

import cv2
import numpy as np

# read the input
img = cv2.imread('newspaper.jpg')
hh, ww = img.shape[:2]

# threshold on white and invert
low = (230,230,230)
high = (255,255,255)
thresh = cv2.inRange(img, low, high)
thresh = 255 - thresh

# apply morphology open to remove noise
kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_RECT , (3,3))
morph = cv2.morphologyEx(thresh, cv2.MORPH_OPEN, kernel)

# get contours
contours = cv2.findContours(morph, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
contours = contours[0] if len(contours) == 2 else contours[1]

# filter contours by area, width, height and aspect ratio (for squareness)
result = img.copy()
cntr_img = img.copy()
for c in contours:
    area = cv2.contourArea(c)
    x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(c)
    cv2.drawContours(cntr_img, [c], 0, (0,0,255), 2)
    if area > 1000 and w < 0.7*ww and h < 0.7*hh and w/h > 0.8 and w/h < 1.2:
        cv2.drawContours(result,[c],0,(0,0,255),2)

# save images
cv2.imwrite('newspaper_thresh.jpg', thresh)
cv2.imwrite('newspaper_morph.jpg', morph)
cv2.imwrite('newspaper_contours.jpg', cntr_img)
cv2.imwrite('newspaper_result.jpg', result)

# show the images
cv2.imshow('thresh', thresh)
cv2.imshow('morph', morph)
cv2.imshow('contours', cntr_img)
cv2.imshow('result', result)
cv2.waitKey(0)
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

Q: Which approaches should be used for monthly demand forecasting with few observations per product? A:

How are you defining "not satisfactory"?

Seems to me the models you chose are fine, I'd even try just a simple linear extrapolation with no library just to see how it would come out. You could also try to do an extrapolation for each month, e.g. use data for January each year etc. since perhaps people buy things at different times of the year.

It is also possible it's just not enough data.

Note I'm not a ML or data expert of any kind.

Q: Kusto range function Semantic error: '' has the following semantic error: Unresolved reference binding:XXX" A:

You're hitting limitations of user-defined functions, as they're documented here: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/kusto/query/functions/user-defined-functions#restrictions-on-the-use-of-user-defined-functions

you should be able to achieve your goal by doing something like the following (matching the example you provided):

let count_by_incident_id = 
    Incidents 
    | summarize count() by IncidentId
;
range idx from 0 to 11 step 1
| join hint.strategy = broadcast (count_by_incident_id)
    on $left.idx == $right.IncidentId
